input: validate the develop skill while its metadata.team names a team that does not exist (platform-engineering, a deleted crew)
expected: the deterministic validator flags a metadata.team that does not resolve to a staffed roster in the federated library
was: _skill_validate never checked metadata.team, so develop's dangling platform-engineering pointer passed its own gate silently
lesson: a skill's metadata.team, when present, must resolve to a staffed roster across the agent homes, and brain.command's _skill_validate enforces it

input: package develop.skill and install it on claude.ai while the skill template manifest is still named templates/skill/SKILL.md
expected: the bundle contains exactly one file named SKILL.md (the manifest at the skill root) and installs cleanly
was: the package shipped two files named SKILL.md (develop/SKILL.md and templates/skill/SKILL.md, the skill template whose frontmatter was the placeholder name: [skill-name]), so the install failed
lesson: a skill bundle must contain exactly one file named SKILL.md, at the skill root; template manifests are named t-SKILL.md so they never collide, and brain.command rejects a second SKILL.md in _skill_validate
